comments.author: CountryOk4844
comments.body:
I don't know what exactly you meant by the hard part, but if you meant marketing and selling it then I don't think it's hard. It's practically impossible. This exact same game idea has been implemented many times before, probably better in some cases, I don't really know because I never found it interesting enough to download any of them even for free, but that just proves my point even more. You simply can't sell the 100th clone of a game that wasn't great to begin with unless you really make it unique and fun, which you didn't.

So I think the hard part is the emotional detachment, acknowledging that this has no value as a game, the only value is the experience you gained while working on it, and move on to your next project (hopefully something with at least a tiny bit of originality so there's a chance someone else will want to play it).

Sorry if it sounds harsh, I'm actually trying to help.

replies.author: Deon_007
replies.body: Yeh I agree with you, i learn lots of things I definitely implement those in next game dev and try something unique this was my first project so I tried something that is easy and already popular.
